findings.summary: Spec §2.1 carries a ⛔ constraint that MinerU calls must use `--noproxy '*'` and clear `http_proxy`/`https_proxy`, because mihomo intercepts internal connections and returns 502. src/mineru.ts issues a bare fetch() with no proxy neutralization, and a repo-wide search finds `noproxy`/`http_proxy` only inside the spec itself — the constraint exists nowhere in code. I do not charge this to the implementer: spec lines 188-190 rule that any ⛔ prose qualifier lacking a corresponding row in the §6 acceptance table is a spec defect, and this constraint has no E-row while E1-E20 are all satisfied. Independently reached; it coincides with the Continuous reviewer's note. The next spec revision should close the table gap before any real MinerU traffic flows.

Spec §7.1 discipline #2 forbids describe block names that enumerate multiple criterion IDs, because the block name pollutes every enclosed test's full name and lets test-name-based mutation attribution cross-match between assertions. Three blocks violate it: `N1 digest dedup (E1/E3)`, `N1 extension hard routing (E6/E7)` (test/mineru.test.ts:72), and `N1 MinerU failure marks the clue blocked (E11/E12)` (test/ingest.test.ts:307). Like the proxy constraint, §7.1 has no §6 E-row, so under the spec's own lines 188-190 this is a spec-table gap rather than an implementer defect. The self-check attribution table in the dev note is nonetheless per-assertion and correct, so the practical risk of a false-positive mutation kill did not materialize here.

`IngestDeps.readExistingTranscript` and `markBlocked` remain injected abstract methods, and no code in `src/` composes the concrete `readExistingTranscript(scanFn, digest)` (src/ingest.ts:160) or `fileParse` (src/mineru.ts:39) with the bus client into a live `IngestDeps` — the node's parts all exist but are never assembled at an entry point, and `transcribeMaterial` is unreferenced outside tests. This does not repeat the §0.2 death cause: all three remediation items the spec demands are genuinely present (pure `buildDigestIndex`, paginated `after_seq` scan, non-abstract composed `readExistingTranscript`), E17/E18/E19 assert against literal data and a stubbed HTTP layer rather than a stub of the dedup core, and no §6 row requires production wiring. Recorded so the follow-up package that assembles the node does not assume the binding already exists.

The dedup read at `transcribeMaterial` happens outside the serialization mutex, so two materials sharing one digest submitted in the same `transcribeBatch` would both miss the index and both reach MinerU — the queue serializes them but does not collapse them. Spec E3 covers only the sequential case and E13 uses distinct digests, so this is outside the acceptance table and correctly not a defect against this package. It is worth noting because the whole point of the digest gate is the GPU cost moat, and an intra-batch duplicate is the one shape that slips past it.
